chunks: From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, who said:

I said to Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who performs the Maghrib salat (prayer) after some of the twilight has disappeared? He said: For a reason, there is no harm. I said: And a man who performs the later 'Isha' salat (prayer) before the twilight disappears? He said: For a reason, there is no harm.

key_terms.الشَّفَقِ: the twilight glow that marks a legal time boundary for prayer
key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the later 'Isha' salat (prayer), the night prayer
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.لِعِلَّةٍ: due to a reason, excuse, or valid cause

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray Maghrib late or 'Isha' early due to an excuse?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the timing of Maghrib and the later 'Isha' salat (prayer). Imam Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام states that performing either outside its usual time boundary due to an excuse or reason carries no harm, indicating legal allowance in cases of necessity.
